study_identification.title: Beyond homogeneity: charting the landscape of heterogeneity in neurodevelopmental and psychiatric electroencephalography

study_characteristics.study_objective: Quantify individual heterogeneity in EEG within neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders using normative modeling on spectral power and functional connectivity; assess improvements over case–control analyses and links to clinical measures.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Permutation tests for overlap differences (5,000 iterations) with FDR correction; Network-based statistics (NBS) comparing groups using original features vs z-score matrices; correlation of global deviation score with clinical assessments (e.g., ADOS).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Normative modeling of EEG reveals highly heterogeneous, frequency-dependent deviations in patients; NM-derived deviations enhance group comparisons and relate to clinical measures, supporting precision psychiatry applications.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Deviation spatial overlap across patients did not exceed ~40% for spectral power and ~24% for connectivity. Patients exhibited significantly greater counts of extreme deviations than HC in several bands (permutation/NBS analyses). A global deviation score (average z over extreme channels/connections) correlated with clinical assessments (e.g., ADOS in ASD).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Aggregate demographics (mean/SD age; sex proportions) for groups not numerically reported; QC procedures beyond impedance checks not detailed; cross-sectional, multi-site EEG may retain residual confounds; external-domain validation/calibration not performed.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Used GAMLSS with band-specific distribution families; fractional-polynomial age effects and heteroscedasticity; z-score matrices fed into NBS; defined global deviation score as subject-level summary; code publicly available.

general_notes.general_notes: Datasets: HBN; MIPDB; ABCCT; femaleASD; LausanneASD. Code: https://github.com/MINDIG-1/NM-Psy. Distribution families vary by band (e.g., SEP/BCPE/ST3/exGAUS); see Suppl. Tables S4–S6.
